title: 他与她的梦 16他与她的梦 15
lines: 格林从碎裂的书架间走出来。
他的脚步比刚才更重了，鞋底踩在那些散落的书页上，发出干燥的碎裂声。暗色的液体从他的拳头上滴落，在地板上留下一条断续的痕迹。
他走过一排又一排书架。
没有爱丽丝。
他经过那些空荡荡的阅读区。
没有爱丽丝。
他推开一扇又一扇门、教室、储藏室，还有自习室。
也没有爱丽丝！
格林的脚步越来越快，至于那些游荡在走廊里的、穿着破旧校服的身影？
它们或许曾经是这所学校的学生，如今只剩下空洞的躯壳。它们漫无目的地走着，偶尔停下来，用一种什么都看不见的目光望向虚空。
格林没有绕开它们，他走过去，伸出手，抓住离他最近的一个学生。那东西被拎起来，双脚离地，微微挣扎了一下。格林看了一眼那张模糊的脸——然后松开手，一掌拍在它的胸口。
那东西飞出去，撞上走廊尽头的墙壁，滑落下来，不再动弹。
格林继续走。
又一个身影从侧面的门里出现。他的拳头已经挥出去了——在看清那个身影之前——但就在拳头即将命中那颗头颅的时候，他看见了什么。
金色的头发？
蓝色的绸带？
爱丽丝？
格林的拳头在最后一刻偏转了方向，他没有打中那个身影的头，而是用力在它的肩侧推了一把。
那个学生飞了出去，滚了几圈，最后躺在地上。它的身体微微抽搐着，但那些抽搐在片刻之后停下了——它只是躺在那里，像一具被丢弃的木偶。
格林停下来，他低头看了那个女学生一眼。
金色的头发——但不是爱丽丝那种明亮的金，而是浅淡的、像是褪色的那种颜色。蓝色的绸带——但是松垮的，像是被人随便系上去的。
格林站在那里，看了几秒钟。
“长得有点像……”他说。声音很轻。不知道是在对谁说，然后他转身，继续向前走去。
身后那个学生躺在地上，一动不动。
格林走过一间又一间教室。他把那些游荡的身影一个个拍开——有的击中胸口，有的击中肩膀，有的只是被他一把推向旁边，让它们撞上墙壁。
他没有用全力，免得让自己满身是血或者什么魔法点燃学院，那个像爱丽丝的人偶他还想要让爱丽丝看看。
那些身影倒下去之后大多还能动，但格林没有再管它们。他只是走过它们，走过那些破碎的桌椅，走过那些空荡荡的黑板，走过那些被遗忘在角落里的书本和笔记。
他没有找到爱丽丝，然后他看见了楼梯，通往楼上的。
格林走上去，脚步声在空旷的楼梯间里回荡，一声一声的，很稳。
二楼的走廊和一楼差不多，只是更加破败。天花板有大片大片的剥落，露出里面的木条。墙壁上有深色的污渍，像是曾经有什么东西在这里被拖拽过。
窗外的月光照进来，在地板上投下长长的、倾斜的光影。
其实格林之前就想要问了，为什么这个学校里的月亮这么圆？而且这么亮？和其他地方看到的月亮完全不一样，非常特别。
content_en:
Greene stepped out from among the shattered bookshelves.
His steps were heavier than before, and the soles of his shoes made a dry crackling sound on the scattered pages. Dark liquid dripped from his fist, leaving an intermittent trail on the floor.
He walked past row after row of bookshelves.
No Alice.
He passed the empty reading areas.
No Alice.
He opened doors after doors, classrooms, storage rooms, and study rooms.
No Alice either!
Green's pace is getting faster and faster. As for those figures wearing shabby school uniforms wandering in the corridor?
They may have been students of this school, but now only empty bodies remain. They walked aimlessly, stopping occasionally and looking into the void with eyes that couldn't see anything.
Green did not go around them. He walked over, stretched out his hand, and grabbed the nearest student. The thing was picked up, its feet lifted off the ground, and it struggled slightly. Green glanced at the blurry face - then let go of his hand and slapped it on the chest.
The thing flew out, hit the wall at the end of the corridor, slid down, and stopped moving.
Greene kept walking.
Another figure appeared from the side door. His fist had already been punched out - before he could see the figure clearly - but just when his fist was about to hit the head, he saw something.
Blonde hair?
Blue ribbon?
Alice?
Green's fist deflected at the last moment. He didn't hit the figure's head, but pushed it hard on the shoulder.
The student flew out, rolled several times, and finally lay on the ground. Its body twitched slightly, but those twitches stopped after a moment - it just lay there, like a discarded puppet.
Green stopped and glanced down at the female student.
Blonde hair—but not Alice's bright blonde, but a light, faded color. The blue ribbon - but loose, as if someone had tied it casually.
"..."
Green stood there and watched for a few seconds.
"It looks a bit like..." he said. The voice is very soft. Not knowing who he was talking to, he turned around and continued walking forward.
The student behind him was lying on the ground, motionless.
Green walked from classroom to classroom. He slapped the wandering figures away one by one - some hit them in the chest, some in the shoulders, and some were just pushed aside by him, causing them to hit the wall.
He didn't use all his strength to avoid being covered in blood or igniting the academy with some magic. He still wanted to show Alice the doll that looked like Alice.
Most of those figures could still move after they fell, but Green ignored them. He just walked past them, past those broken tables and chairs, past those empty blackboards, past those books and notes forgotten in the corner.
He didn't find Alice, and then he saw the stairs leading upstairs.
Green walked up, his footsteps echoing in the empty stairwell, one after another, very steady.
The corridors on the second floor are similar to those on the first floor, only more dilapidated. The ceiling was peeling off in large swaths, exposing the wooden slats inside. There were dark stains on the walls, as if something had been dragged there.
The moonlight from the window came in, casting long, sloping shadows on the floor.
In fact, Green had wanted to ask before, why is the moon in this school so round? And so bright? It is completely different from the moon seen elsewhere, very special.
